page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz, with 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 120.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.5 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA Pascal-generation P100 GPUs with a combined total of 32 GB VRAM. Local storage consists of a 944 GB SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a 5 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 954.09 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 21.45 GB/sec, both placing in the lower percentiles. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 9532.02 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 59.76 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is stable, reaching 683.87 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 56.56 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Redis SET operations perform at 10.88 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 9.91 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dual dedicated enterprise GPUs and local SSD storage offsets the older Intel Xeon CPU architecture. This hardware profile is best suited for workloads that offload heavy computations to the GPU rather than relying on high single-core CPU performance. Appropriate workloads include legacy GPU-accelerated deep learning training, parallel scientific simulations, video transcoding, and database operations that benefit from local SSD storage and moderate multi-core processing.
